newsitem.title: UK: Copper above $2,300 on LME, at six-month highs.
newsitem.headline: Copper above $2,300 on LME, at six-month highs.

text.p: Copper prices broke above the $2,300 a tonne level during early London Metal Exchange (LME) trading on Thursday, hitting fresh six-month highs of $2,306/2,310.
Traders said the market rose quickly from overnight closing levels of $2,264/68, breaking the previous high of $2,285 set on Tuesday and triggering pre-set buy-orders.
Traders added that impetus for the gains came from overnight news that stocks of metal in U.S. warehouses had fallen, which underlined the critically-low level of inventories worldwide.
LME warehouse stocks of copper stand at 6-1/4 year lows of just 90,050 tonnes, and this dearth of metal has resulted in soaring premiums for immediate supplies.
The premium or backwardation for cash metal over three months is now at $280/290 a tonne, up from $270 yesterday.
Analysts expected the market to remain volatile, and said prices could rise much further as buying against options would also be triggered by this advance.
